reading.body:
DartPoints Charleston in Ladson, South Carolina, publishes 1.3 MW of IT capacity, operated by DartPoints.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 130 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 32 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

No compliance certifications are published for DartPoints Charleston. That does not mean none exist, only that this site's dataset, built from the operator's own facility page, does not list any, which limits what regulated workloads a reader could confirm the facility is qualified to host.

South Carolina has 4 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 4 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 6.6 MW. DartPoints Charleston contributes 1.3 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
